# Deliberately broken. Used ONLY by `lint-actions.sh --self-test`, which asserts
# that each of the three rules fires on it by name.
#
# It lives in its own file, with an extension the linter does not collect, for
# two reasons: the linter must not lint its own fixture, and holding these
# literals inside lint-actions.sh made that script trip its own rules the moment
# the script itself came into scope. Three run: blocks, one broken rule each,
# plus rule (4) in a DESCRIPTION rather than a run: block -- which is where the
# real instance was, and why rule (4) is a whole-file scan instead of a yq walk
# over the keys the other rules look at.
name: deliberately bad
description: >
  rule (4): an empty GitHub expression, ${{ }}, in a YAML value. On a real
  action this fails the whole file to load before any step runs.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    # rule (3): producer piped into an early-exiting consumer.
    - shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        tar tzf "$F" | grep -q '^variants/windows-x86_64/'
    # rule (2): GitHub interpolation substituted into the script text.
    - shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        if [ -z "${{ inputs.smoke }}" ]; then echo no; fi
    # rule (1): a plain shellcheck finding (SC2086 etc).
    - shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        if [ $UNQUOTED == x ]; then echo hi; fi
